doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Hating his own recorded voice; learning to sing
summary: He heard his father in his voice and took years to learn to use the microphone as a non-natural vocalist.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well the first time I had earphones on I didn’t like it at all. I thought I sounded like my father, which was very problematic for me. I heard my father’s voice in my own voice, and I had never heard that. But yeah, and it took years frankly, ‘cause I’m not a natural vocalist. I, you know, sang and do sing, continue to sing, because it’s a way to present certain musical ideas, but I didn’t start out wanting to be a vocalist or a singer and I had © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

never put any time into learning to use my voice, and particularly with the microphone. You know these microphones today, you can really work with them to project a certain persona or image, they’re so sensitive that you can’t do in the real world. It’s like working with a microphone. And that’s this whole territory that opens up for you once you get into a studio.
